coverage_notes: All registered anchors on PDF pp.5-8 were visually viewed along with material/method text and Table 2. PDF pp.1-2 are library cover sheets; p.3 title confirms the paper identity. No crevice-corrosion potentials were substituted for pitting results.
shared_qualifications: C16: K -273.15 gives C. The source uses rounded engineering pairs: 333 K about 60 C, 353 K about 80 C and 373 K about 100 C (exact arithmetic 59.85,79.85,99.85). Source sweep 20 mV/min /60=0.333333 mV/s, compatible with CRA 0.3333. V vs SCE x1000 gives mV vs SCE; no reference offset is needed.

Figure 7 upward arrows at 1.0 V are registered lower testing limits. CRA encodes these as numerical Avg values 1000-1020 mV. Their material/temperature identities are supported, but the source bound does not establish those exact central values; potential_agreement is not_comparable for those links.

Table 2 (PDF p.5) distinguishes 28Cr, 2942, 254 and 329J2L base metals. Figure 4 simulated HAZ specimens, Figure 10 ten-second heat treatments, and Figures 11/13 weldments are different conditions, not repetitions of the base-metal temperature series.

The paper names synthetic seawater but does not provide enough recipe information in the inspected passages to independently establish CRA CL- 0.546 M. The original CSV comments explicitly call chloride concentration estimated; that estimate is not used as independent paper evidence.

obs_033 Fig.13 is a base-metal comparison point but its specific test temperature/run correspondence to Fig.7 is not established. Same grade and nearby potentials alone do not support a link. Registered weld-presentation ambiguities and the 12 versus 13.5 kJ/cm source difference are retained without consolidating observations.
